text.project-1.title: ESP32 IoT Node — Embedded QA Case Study
text.project-1.desc: Risk-based testing of an ESP32 IoT node in Wokwi: Master Test Plan, 32 tests in the matrix, 39 Pytest tests over UART, I2C analysis in PulseView. Found 9 Critical and 14 Major defects; release decision: NO-GO. Documents: Bug reports ↗ · Test plan ↗ · Test matrix ↗
text.project-ai-api.title: API testing of an AI website builder
text.project-ai-api.desc: For the last few months I tested the API of a service that uses AI to generate and clone WordPress websites: sent generation requests and checked the resulting websites by comparing copies with the originals. Checked SEO metadata (og, hreflang, canonical), robots.txt and sitemap, server response headers, internal links and bot protection, using AI tools for testing. Found about 10 defects and mismatches: the old domain left in metadata and robots.txt, lost robots.txt rules, links returning 404, and missing bot protection on the copy. The project is under NDA and still in development.
text.project-monitoring.title: Website monitoring SaaS
text.project-monitoring.desc: A real-time website monitoring service: availability checks every 15 minutes from several countries, site errors, Google Safe Browsing status, SSL and domain expiration, PageSpeed Insights and redirect checks. My role: testing, participation in development, feature ideas. The project is under NDA; details on request at the interview.
text.project-3.title: n8n automations for SEO
text.project-3.desc: Three production automations: submitting pages for fast indexing via API, monitoring sitemap.xml every 15 minutes and submitting only new and updated pages (lastmod comparison, n8n Data Tables, Telegram alerts), and collecting Google rankings via DataForSEO into Google Sheets — a rank-tracking service was built on top of this flow. Tested webhooks and requests in Postman: sent requests and verified the results.
text.project-2.title: Offline Voice Assistant
text.project-2.desc: A fully offline Ukrainian voice assistant on Orange Pi Zero 3: VAD → Vosk (STT) → commands / local LLM → Piper (TTS). Includes a documented hardware debugging journey.
text.project-security.tag: NDA · Security testing · OWASP ZAP · Burp Suite · Google Dorks
text.project-security.title: Web security testing
text.project-security.desc: Automated vulnerability scanning with OWASP ZAP (Zed Attack Proxy) and Burp Suite, plus searching with Google Dorks. Checked the company’s corporate websites, in-house WordPress themes and websites of prospective clients. Found exposed service files and vulnerable plugins; everything found was fixed by the team. The project is under NDA; details on request at the interview.
text.project-wp-themes.title: WordPress products: platform, plugins, themes
text.project-wp-themes.desc:
Several WordPress products where I combined PM, tester and feature-ideas roles:
— a security and maintenance platform for WordPress websites and PBNs: layered protection, backups to three storages, monitoring of 11 parameters, cache purging via API. Role: project curator;
— a security plugin: firewall, 2FA, CAPTCHA, hardening. Role: testing on live websites, feature ideas, partial management of development and testing;
— about 30 themes and 3 plugins: testing and assigning fixes to HTML/CSS developers, designers and developers.
Stack: PHP, MySQL, Bash/Linux. The projects are under NDA; details on request at the interview.
text.project-wp-cloning.title: Bulk WordPress site deployment
text.project-wp-cloning.desc: Designed a process for cloning and bulk-deploying websites built on the same templates with the Duplicator WordPress plugin, and trained colleagues to follow it. About 3,000 websites were deployed this way, cutting the time to create a website roughly in half.
text.exp-qa.desc: Alongside my main role, tested the company’s products: about 10 websites, 3 plugins (including a WordPress security plugin), about 30 WordPress themes, a website monitoring SaaS, a WordPress maintenance platform and the API of an AI website builder. Manual exploratory testing on live websites, automated security scanning (OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite, Google Dorks), assigning fixes to developers, HTML/CSS developers and designers, and verifying the fixes. Projects under NDA.
text.about.p3: Why QA: as a PM and Tech Lead I valued release quality the most, and I have been into electronics and embedded since childhood. Since March 2026 I have been studying embedded and deliberately started with QA — to enter the field faster, understand how devices work from the inside, and keep growing in the stack.
text.reco.title: Mentor’s recommendation
text.reco.intro: A LinkedIn recommendation from my Embedded QA course mentor.
text.reco.quote: “Throughout the course, Evhenii demonstrated a strong commitment to learning, analytical thinking, and a structured approach to Embedded QA. I was particularly impressed by his practical work. He successfully worked on several important assignments, including Root Cause Analysis (RCA), a Hardware Validation Report, a Master Test Plan, and a comprehensive portfolio case. Evhenii approached these assignments with responsibility and attention to detail. I believe he has a solid foundation and great potential to grow as an Embedded QA Engineer.”
text.reco.author: Oleh Moroz
text.reco.role: Senior Manual / Automation / Embedded QA, Prometheus mentor · 29.10.2026
